arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__subarray-sum-.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__subarray-sum-.pattern: Prefix sum + hashmap of seen prefix counts
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__subarray-sum-.statement: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the total number of contiguous subarrays whose elements sum to exactly `k`. Values may be negative, so a sliding window does not work.

approaches.name: Prefix sum with hashmap
approaches.idea: A subarray ending at index `i` sums to `k` iff there is an earlier prefix equal to `prefix[i]-k`. Keep a running prefix sum and a map from prefix value to how many times it occurred (seed with `0->1` for the empty prefix). At each element add the count of `prefix-k` to the answer, then record the current prefix. This handles negatives, unlike a window.

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__subarray-sum-.insight: Count subarrays with a target sum by counting earlier prefix sums equal to current_prefix - k.

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__subarrays-wit.title: Subarrays with K Different Integers
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__subarrays-wit.statement: Given an integer array `nums` and integer `k`, return the number of contiguous subarrays that contain exactly `k` distinct integers (a "good" subarray). Counting exactly-k directly is awkward, but exactly-k equals (at-most-k) minus (at-most-(k-1)).

approaches.name: atMost(k) - atMost(k-1)
approaches.idea: `atMost(k)` counts subarrays with at most `k` distinct values using a sliding window: expand `right`, and whenever the window holds more than `k` distinct values shrink from `left`; every window contributes `right-left+1` subarrays ending at `right`. Subarrays with exactly `k` distinct = atMost(k) - atMost(k-1). This converts a hard exact-count into two easy monotone windows.

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__subarrays-wit.insight: Exactly-K distinct = atMost(K) - atMost(K-1); each 'at most' is a clean monotone sliding window.

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__count-of-rang.title: Count of Range Sum
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__count-of-rang.pattern: Prefix sums + merge sort (count inversions in a range)
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__count-of-rang.statement: Given an integer array `nums` and two integers `lower` and `upper`, return the number of range sums `S(i,j) = nums[i]+...+nums[j]` (i <= j) that lie in the inclusive range `[lower, upper]`. Equivalently, count pairs `p < q` of prefix sums with `lower <= prefix[q]-prefix[p] <= upper`.
constraints: prefix sums can overflow int, use long

approaches.name: Merge sort on prefix sums
approaches.idea: Build prefix sums `prefix[0..n]` (use `long`). The answer counts pairs `i<j` with `lower <= prefix[j]-prefix[i] <= upper`. During merge sort of the prefix array, when the left and right halves are each sorted, for every `i` in the left half advance two pointers over the right half to count how many `prefix[j]` fall in `[prefix[i]+lower, prefix[i]+upper]`, then merge. Each level counts cross-pairs in linear time.

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__count-of-rang.insight: Reduce to counting prefix-sum pairs in a value window; a merge sort counts those cross-pairs in O(n log n).

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__maximum-sum-o.title: Maximum Sum of 3 Non-Overlapping Subarrays
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__maximum-sum-o.pattern: Prefix sums + best-left / best-right precompute around a fixed middle
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__maximum-sum-o.statement: Given an integer array `nums` and integer `k`, find three non-overlapping subarrays each of length `k` that have the maximum total sum, and return their starting indices. If several answers tie, return the lexicographically smallest index triple.

examples.explanation: Lexicographically smallest triple among the ties.

approaches.name: Fix the middle window, precompute best left/right
approaches.idea: Precompute each length-`k` window sum via prefix sums. `left[i]` = index of the best window in `[0..i]` (earliest on ties) and `right[i]` = index of the best window in `[i..end]` (earliest on ties, so scan right-to-left with `>=`). Then try every valid middle start `mid`; the best left window is `left[mid-k]` and best right is `right[mid+k]`. Keep the max total, which yields the lexicographically smallest triple because ties always favor the earliest index.

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__maximum-sum-o.insight: Anchor the middle window, then the problem splits into independent best-left and best-right lookups.

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__number-of-sub.title: Number of Submatrices That Sum to Target
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__number-of-sub.pattern: Fix column pair, reduce to 1D Subarray Sum Equals K
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__number-of-sub.statement: Given a 2D matrix and an integer `target`, return the number of non-empty submatrices whose elements sum to `target`. Two submatrices are different if they differ in any coordinate. Reduce the 2D count to repeated 1D subarray-sum-equals-target counts.

examples.explanation: Four submatrices sum to 0 (the four corner cells).

approaches.name: Row prefix sums + hashmap over column pairs
approaches.idea: First turn each row into its horizontal prefix sums, so the sum of row `r` between columns `c1..c2` is O(1). For every column pair `(c1,c2)`, walk down the rows accumulating a running column-band prefix and apply the 1D Subarray-Sum-Equals-K trick: a hashmap of seen band-prefixes lets you count how many earlier rows give a rectangle summing to `target`. This is the matrix analog of prefix + hashmap.

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__number-of-sub.insight: Collapse two of the four rectangle boundaries by fixing a column pair, leaving a 1D subarray-sum-equals-target scan.

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__max-sum-of-re.title: Max Sum of Rectangle No Larger Than K
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__max-sum-of-re.pattern: Fix column pair + TreeSet for max subarray sum <= K
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__max-sum-of-re.statement: Given an `m x n` matrix and an integer `k`, return the maximum sum of any non-empty rectangle whose sum is no larger than `k`. It is guaranteed such a rectangle exists.

examples.explanation: Rectangle [[0,1],[-2,3]] sums to 2, the max sum that is <= 2.

approaches.name: Column-pair compression + TreeSet ceiling
approaches.idea: Fix a pair of columns and compress each row into a single band value, reducing the problem to: max subarray sum <= k in a 1D array. For that, keep a sorted set of seen prefix sums; for a running prefix `p`, the best subarray ending here with sum <= k is `p - ceiling(p-k)`, found via `TreeSet.ceiling`. Track the global best over all column pairs. Iterate the outer loop over the smaller dimension for speed.

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__max-sum-of-re.insight: For 'sum no larger than k', a sorted set of prefix sums plus ceiling(prefix-k) gives the best bounded subarray.

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__continuous-su.title: Continuous Subarray Sum / Subarray Sums Divisible by K
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__continuous-su.pattern: Prefix-sum remainders modulo k in a hashmap
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__continuous-su.statement: Two related problems built on prefix-sum remainders mod `k`. Continuous Subarray Sum: return true if there is a contiguous subarray of length at least 2 whose sum is a multiple of `k`. Subarray Sums Divisible by K: return the count of contiguous subarrays whose sum is divisible by `k`. Both use the fact that two prefixes with the same remainder bound a subarray whose sum is a multiple of `k`.

examples.explanation: [2,4] sums to 6, a multiple of 6, length >= 2.
Seven subarrays have a sum divisible by 5.

constraints: 0 <= nums[i] <= 10^9 (Continuous Subarray Sum); -10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4 (Divisible by K)
normalize remainders with ((x % k) + k) % k to handle negatives

approaches.name: Continuous Subarray Sum: first index of each remainder
approaches.idea: If two prefix sums share the same remainder mod `k`, the subarray between them sums to a multiple of `k`. Store the earliest index at which each remainder appears (seed remainder 0 at index -1). When a remainder repeats and the gap is at least 2, return true. Keeping only the first index maximizes the length gap.

approaches.name: Subarray Sums Divisible by K: count each remainder
approaches.idea: Count subarrays with sum divisible by `k` by counting, for each running remainder, how many earlier prefixes had the same remainder (each such pair bounds a divisible subarray). A size-`k` array of remainder counts (seeded with `count[0]=1` for the empty prefix) does this in one pass. Normalize negatives so remainders stay in `[0,k)`.

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__continuous-su.insight: Equal prefix-sum remainders mod k bound a subarray divisible by k; store first index to test existence, counts to tally.

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__split-array-l.title: Split Array Largest Sum
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__split-array-l.pattern: Binary search on the answer (min feasible largest sum)
arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__split-array-l.statement: Given a non-negative integer array `nums` and integer `k`, split it into `k` non-empty contiguous subarrays so that the largest subarray sum among the splits is minimized, and return that minimized largest sum.

examples.explanation: Split [7,2,5] and [10,8]; largest sum 18 is minimal.

approaches.name: Binary search on the maximum allowed subarray sum
approaches.idea: The answer lies between `max(nums)` (no piece can be smaller than the largest element) and `sum(nums)` (one piece). Binary search this range; for a candidate cap, greedily walk the array opening a new piece whenever adding the next element would exceed the cap, and count how many pieces are needed. If that count is <= k the cap is feasible, so search lower; otherwise search higher. Feasibility is monotone, so binary search converges to the minimum feasible cap.

arrays-hashing-prefix-sum__split-array-l.insight: Minimizing a maximum with a monotone feasibility check is binary search on the answer, greedily counting pieces.
